title: The Obstacles to Presence, Power, and Warmth
coreMove: Diagnose the specific inner obstacle that is leaking into your outward signal.
sourcePressure: The source positions this chapter as diagnostic: obstacles interrupt presence, power, and warmth because internal state shows up in body language and social read.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version labels every problem as nerves. The useful version separates distraction, discomfort, self-attack, irritation, and threat so each can be handled later.

counterintuition: Just get out of your head

exampleSpecs.domain: an animal shelter adoption consult where a coordinator feels judged by a prospective owner
exampleSpecs.audience: a caring reader whose defensiveness blocks warmth
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a cautious adopter trusts the shelter's recommendation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she notices her jaw tightening after the adopter questions the fee, then labels the obstacle as defensiveness before it turns into clipped answers
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a microchip scanner lying beside a leash hook

exampleSpecs.domain: a patent review panel where an inventor loses presence while waiting for a hostile question
exampleSpecs.audience: a technical reader who mistakes anticipation for preparation
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the panel hears the actual claim or only sees bracing
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he watches the recording and circles the moment his eyes left the questioner to scan the room for attack
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a patent diagram projected beside a silent lapel mic

exampleSpecs.domain: a luxury hotel concierge desk during a lost-passport complaint
exampleSpecs.audience: a service professional whose irritation reads as lack of goodwill
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the guest accepts the embassy process without escalating
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the concierge feels the unfair accusation land, notices his smile flatten, and chooses to identify irritation as the obstacle before replying
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a brass room key tag beside an embassy phone number

exampleSpecs.domain: a marine biology field debrief after a failed reef sample dive
exampleSpecs.audience: a leader whose embarrassment weakens power
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the crew trusts the next dive plan
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she identifies shame, not lack of knowledge, as the reason she keeps overexplaining the failed sample grid
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a salt-stiff dive slate drying beside a cracked sample vial

exampleSpecs.domain: an immigration clinic intake where a volunteer is distracted by the line forming behind the client
exampleSpecs.audience: a helper who loses presence while trying to be efficient
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the client shares the detail that changes the filing deadline
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: contrast the rushed intake with the moment she names divided attention as the obstacle and turns the queue number screen away from her sightline
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a numbered intake ticket curled beside a passport photo

exampleSpecs.domain: a fencing bout corner where a coach's own panic makes a cadet more frantic
exampleSpecs.audience: a mentor whose urgent care leaks as alarm
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the cadet can hear one tactical correction before the final touch
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coach hears his voice speed up, recognizes threat contagion as the obstacle, and stops adding three corrections at once
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a red scoring light reflected on a bent foil guard

skillTargets: diagnose which obstacle is weakening presence, power, or warmth
separate internal obstacle from outward symptom
avoid solving before naming the obstacle
analyze how distraction, defensiveness, and threat leak into social read

tryThisNowSpec: In one live exchange today, catch the first sign of a charisma break and name the obstacle privately in three words or fewer.
